Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — rough traffic + SLOs

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking this. We're trying to understand what a Redwood Dedicated commit would look like for our primary inference workloads and what headroom we should plan for. High level:

- Model: open-llm/longform-7b (currently unquantized in our prod tests)
- Expected peak: ~120,000 tokens/sec (9–11AM PST peak from our sample)
- Typical request: ~300 tokens per request, bursty concurrency (spikes up to ~400 simultaneous requests)
- SLO target: p95 generation latency <= 350 ms (customer-facing interactive flows)
- KV/cache hit assumptions: cold-starts matter (we see ~25% cache hit on first byte across users)

I've attached a CSV sample of request timestamps and token counts for the last 72 hours (skorpius_workload_sample.csv).

Questions: what committed slab (H100-equivalent) do you recommend to meet the p95 target with reasonable headroom (we'd like ~25–40% cushion)? Also, how much reduction in committed GPUs can we get if we add a quantized fallback (4-bit) and accept slightly lower quality on very high load?

Can you share a quick note with recommended committed GPUs, suggested burst policy, and any quick ops/cost tradeoffs?

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a call if it helps.

Jordan
Ops Lead
Skorpius Health

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — rough traffic + SLOs

Hi Jordan — thanks for the sample. I ran a quick sizing pass with our profiler and a lightweight capacity model (attached: minacalc_sizing_model.xlsx). Key assumptions I used:

- Baseline measured throughput: longform-7b (fp16) ~15k tokens/sec per H100 when serving 300-token avg requests with 64ms average token generation time in our test harness and a continuous batching window of 6–8ms.
- Quantized (4-bit) fallback improves throughput ~1.9x in our bench (estimate ~28.5k tokens/sec/H100) but increases variance and can worsen some failure modes; quality delta is moderate.
- Cache/KV warm hit: when cache hit rate >65% we see effective latency drop by ~18–22% (this mostly helps p50, some p95 benefit).

Quick recommendations:

- Committed slab: 9 H100-equivalent GPUs (9 * 15k = 135k tokens/sec nominal). This provides nominal headroom above your 120k peak and gives ~12.5% buffer for short bursts.
- SLO cushion: to reach a robust p95 <= 350ms under realistic burst noise and cold cache seasons, target commit of 12 H100-equivalents (12 * 15k = 180k tokens/sec) to achieve ~50% headroom. This is conservative but aligns with a 30–50% cushion you mentioned.
- Cost/fallback trade: with a quantified fallback you can operate a smaller committed slab (8 H100) + 2 H100-equivalent burst-capacity on demand, and automatically fallback to quantized model if queue depth crosses threshold. This reduces steady-state committed spend by ~18% at the expense of occasional quality degradation on heavy spikes.

Proposed mutual action plan:
- We can run a 72-hour pilot on a mixed slab (8 committed H100 + 2 burst H100) and instrument p95/p99.
- If we see p95 misses > 2% during the pilot, we perform a one-time uplift to 10–12 committed H100 per the conservative plan.

I've attached the sizing workbook and a starter pricing sketch (sr-pricing-proposal.pdf). If this looks reasonable I'll loop in Billing/CS to formalize commitment pricing and SLA language.

Would you be available for a 30-min call Monday to walk through the workbook?

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

My model suggests 9 H100 nominal covers the reported 120k tokens/sec but we should bake in more cushion for:
- traffic pattern uncertainty (their sample shows heavy short spikes),
- cold-cache effects during regional launches, and
- p95 tail sensitivity to batching variability.

Ben: can you sanity-check the 15k tokens/sec/H100 baseline? If we assume a 20% lower throughput in-prod (noisy tails), we may want to recommend 10–12 H100 committed to avoid a second uplift.
Rishi: for the fallback path, what's your ops estimate to support automated fallback to the 4-bit variant (monitoring + rollback playbook)? Also, how quickly can we scale burst capacity in their region?

My leaning: propose the pilot (8 committed + 2 burst) but include explicit uplift gates in the MAP and a 30-day SLA clause that allows a single uplift after pilot metrics. That reduces friction to sign while protecting SLOs.

— Mina

Mina — 15k/H100 looks reasonable for the workload profile (7B with ~300 token average) when using our tight batching configuration and 6–8ms batching window. In noisy production we see 10–12k tokens/sec/H100 more commonly; recommend we present both optimistic (15k) and conservative (12k) numbers to the customer.

If we show both: pilot = 8 committed + 2 burst (optimistic), conservative commit = 11 H100 (using 12k baseline) — that gives ~132k tokens/sec. With 30% cushion that's 171k target which maps to 14 H100. We should pick the conservative commit for procurement asks.

— Ben

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — tokens/sec reconciliation & proposal

Jordan — thanks again for the sample and patience while we did an internal sanity check. Below is a concise, actionable proposal based on profiling and ops constraints.

Executive recommendation (two paths):

1) Pilot-first (faster to sign):
- Commit: 8 H100-equivalents (committed slab)
- Burst: 2 H100-equivalent burst capacity (soft-burst pool)
- Fallback: quantized 4-bit model automatically enabled when queue depth threshold exceeded
- Expected nominal capacity (optimistic profiler): 8 * 15k = 120k t/s; burst adds ~30k t/s short term.
- Pilot deliverable: instrumented 72-hour run, p95/p99 telemetry, acceptance criteria: p95 <= 350ms <= 98% of sample windows.

2) Conservative commit (procurement-friendly, single-step):
- Commit: 12 H100-equivalents (12 * 12k conservative baseline = 144k t/s nominal, ~50% headroom vs reported 120k peak when accounting for noisy tails)
- No fallback required for sign-off, but we still recommend enabling quantized variant as an escape hatch.

Ops notes and rationale:
- We present both numbers to Procurement so they can choose speed-to-production (pilot path) vs single-step SLA guarantee (conservative).
- If you accept the pilot path we require explicit uplift gates in the MAP: if p95 misses >2% over pilot, Redwood will upgrade committed slab to the conservative commit within 7 business days (pre-agreed uplift pricing applies).
- Runbook: we will enable cache-warm policies (prefix warming) and a 15-min emergency burst activation window for the soft-burst pool. Rishi will be primary ops contact for the pilot.

Next steps
- If you want to proceed: sign the attached starter SR proposal and we schedule the pilot.
- Optional: book a 30-min technical walkthrough of the sizing workbook Monday PST.

Thanks — I put Ben, Rishi on the thread for ops/pricing sanity checks. Happy to adjust based on your procurement preferences.

Best,
